column1: # Android's own labels, read from the phone at run time (ADR 0054): for each label Datapavan quotes, the places to read
# it from, tried in order, a maker's rows before the aosp rows. Columns, by tabs:
#   key       the label, as Datapavan's code names it (its fallback string is android_label_KEY);
#   maker     aosp, for any phone, or a maker as Build.MANUFACTURER gives it, in lower case;
#   api       the Android versions it holds for: 29- (29 and later), 30-30 (Android 11 only), 31-35;
#   package   a package name, which must be a system app: for an aosp row, Settings (com.android.settings, which also
#             holds SettingsLib's strings) or the permission controller (Google's or AOSP's);
#   name      the resource's name in that package;
#   verified  the model and build of a device whose screen showed the label under that name, or -; a maker's row always
#   source    aosp:REPOSITORY@FIRST..LAST, the AOSP repository (SOURCE) and the tags its name was read at, or device.
# Names only: the labels' texts are each phone's, read from its own Settings. A label read through an aosp row counts
# as the phone's own only on a maker whose Settings show AOSP's labels (SystemLabels.AOSP_MAKERS: google, for Pixels
# and the emulators); on any other maker it is worded as Android's name until that maker's own verified row says the
# name is the one its screen shows.
# Samsung, read on a Galaxy A40 (SM-A405FN, One UI 3, Android 11, build A405FNXXU4CWC3) on 2026-11-22: its Settings keep
# AOSP's names, and the screen showed the text read through them, in English, for these ten.
